name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with PVI of D+24
Incumbent Alma Adams running for reelection
Republican challenger has minimal fundraising and no cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Adams holds a D+24 district with the advantages of incumbency and a large cash edge, while her opponent has raised under $30,000 and has essentially no money to compete. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an unexpectedly strong national Republican wave environment could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 12th District is a heavily Democratic, majority-Black Charlotte-area seat where Alma Adams has been reelected comfortably since 2014. The district's partisan lean of D+24 makes a Republican win extremely unlikely under any normal circumstance.

Adams enters the race with about $457,000 on hand, while Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $30,000 and reported just $3 in cash, leaving him little ability to run a visible campaign. No independent polls of the race exist, but prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%. The forecast calls this seat Safe Democratic, with Adams expected to win by roughly 26 points.
